output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents actually stayed at about 37 a month in September and October, close to the old average. Of these, 47 were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" after analysts had confirmed them. Each move happened 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 4-hour SLA warning flag appeared. The moves came from the Brackwater integration account, driven by a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host that polls for cases with the SLA warning every 5 minutes and then patches the category. It is not a platform fault, because the connector itself wrote no categories. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater shows 100% SLA compliance and its bonus looks triggered. The monitoring queue has grown to about 96 cases. Most of the 47 have no containment recorded.

Do not cut the IR retainer or sign off the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have your in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-write rights from the Brackwater role. Then demand a written explanation from Brackwater before renewal. Hold off on service credits until containment is checked. I could not tell whether the 28 dropped detection rules are hiding attacks. That needs its own review. Confidence in the main finding is high.
